metadata.title: System Security and Privacy Plan – Secure High-Performance Computing Platform

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: System designed and governed in accordance with NIST SP 800-234 (High-Performance Computing Security Guide).

system-characteristics.description: A shared, scheduler-mediated high-performance computing platform designed for research and institutional workloads, emphasizing explicit trust boundaries, job lifecycle security, data protection, and governed performance trade-offs.

authorization-boundary.description: Includes all compute nodes, schedulers, shared storage, accelerators, interconnect fabrics, identity systems, and security monitoring components used to deliver HPC services.

users.title: HPC User
users.description: Authorized internal or federated users submitting non-interactive batch jobs.

users.title: HPC Administrator
users.description: Privileged operators responsible for platform operation and maintenance.

components.title: Secure High-Performance Computing (Composite Trust)
components.description: Composite trust assertion for secure HPC operation.

implemented-components.description: Shared-node execution trust and scheduler-mediated control.
Job attribution, scheduler authority, and role separation.
Job submission, execution context control, and lifecycle governance.
Shared storage access control, job data isolation, and residual data risk management.
Interconnect, RDMA, accelerator isolation, and residual execution state mitigation.
Detection of anomalous or malicious but policy-compliant job behavior.
Explicit governance of performance-driven security trade-offs.
Federated identity trust and accountability (if applicable).

control-implementation.description: Controls are satisfied by platform trust patterns asserted via secure-hpc. Detailed control-to-pattern mappings are provided in component definitions rather than duplicated in this SSP.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Access control requirements are satisfied via hpc-identity-and-access and hpc-job-lifecycle-security.
System and communication protections are satisfied via hpc-core and hpc-fabric-and-accelerator-trust.
System integrity monitoring and behavioral detection are satisfied via hpc-behavioral-monitoring.
Availability and resource fairness controls are satisfied via hpc-core and scheduler mediation.
Audit and accountability are satisfied via scheduler logs, job attribution, and behavioral monitoring.

authorization-boundary.description: Authorization applies to all shared compute, scheduling, and data services delivered under the HPC platform.
